lesson_title: Your Compass Is Lying to You — By a Known, Growing Angle
hook_text: Every compass in South Africa points at the wrong north. Geography teaches you to correct the lie.
clip_script: Put a map flat on the table and lay an imaginary compass on top of it. The map points at true north — the top of the planet, the pole every map in the world agrees on. The needle could not care less about the map: it swings to its own north, the magnetic one, which from South Africa lies off to the west. Two arrows on one table, pointing at two different norths, with a wedge of angle between them. That wedge is magnetic declination — the size of the compass's lie. And the lie will not even hold still: the magnetic pole drifts as the deep Earth churns, so the wedge stretches a few minutes wider each year.
visual_style: Top-down shot of a topographic map with two animated arrows splitting apart — one labelled TRUE, one labelled MAGNETIC — the wedge between them ticking wider year by year, ending on the 18 degrees 25 minutes answer line.
mood: Conspiratorial reveal turning into a satisfying step-by-step fix.
pacing: Slow reveal of the two arrows, quick-fire calculation beats, clean stamp on the final answer.
